prompt: A private equity firm is deciding whether to buy a chain of veterinary clinics. The candidate's framework: (1) The target's financial performance; (2) The target's revenue growth and margins; (3) Attractiveness of the vet clinic market; (4) Synergies with the firm's other pet businesses. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 2 overlap: growth and margins are financial performance
options.feedback: Right. Revenue growth and margins are part of financial performance, so bucket 2 repeats bucket 1. Use the slot for the deal terms: price, financing and exit.

options.text: Missing: how fast the vet clinic market is growing
options.feedback: Market growth is part of the market's attractiveness, which bucket 3 covers.

options.text: Bucket 4 doesn't belong: a PE firm values each target on its own
options.feedback: The firm owns other pet businesses. Shared purchasing or referrals can justify a higher price, so synergies matter here.

options.text: It's a generic due-diligence list: it never asks why vet clinics
options.feedback: Bucket 3 asks exactly that: how attractive the vet clinic market is. The flaw is the overlap between buckets 1 and 2.

explanation: Financial performance already includes growth and margins. A cleaner structure: market, target performance, synergies, and deal economics (price, financing, exit).

extras.corrected_framework: Market attractiveness; target performance; synergies; deal economics (price, financing, exit)
